baslik: Surprise AWS bill, how do I find what's costing money and stop it?
soru: I got a much bigger AWS bill than expected this month. I'm a solo dev and thought I was within free tier. I don't even know what's running. How do I find what's generating cost and make sure I shut down anything I'm not using, without breaking something I need?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: Start in Cost Explorer and group by Service, then by Region. This immediately shows whether it's EC2, RDS, NAT Gateway, data transfer, etc. A huge number of 'surprise bill' posts come down to: a NAT Gateway (hourly + data charges), an idle RDS instance, an Elastic IP not attached to a running instance, or resources in a region you forgot about.

Check EVERY region, not just your usual one. The console defaults to one region but resources (and bills) accumulate per region. Use the Billing console's cost breakdown, and check for running EC2/RDS in regions you never intended to use, sometimes from a tutorial or a compromised key.

If the jump is sudden and large, rule out compromised credentials, leaked access keys get used to spin up huge EC2 fleets for crypto mining. Check CloudTrail for unfamiliar RunInstances calls, rotate keys immediately, and contact AWS Support, they often waive fraud-related charges.
Set up a Budget with an alert (Billing > Budgets) so you get emailed when spend crosses a threshold, this prevents future surprises. Free-tier alerts are also available.
Mine was a NAT Gateway I'd left running from a tutorial, about $32/month doing nothing. Deleting it and setting a $5 budget alert fixed the bleed and warns me now.

cozum: Start in Cost Explorer and group by Service, then by Region. This immediately shows whether it's EC2, RDS, NAT Gateway, data transfer, etc. A huge number of 'surprise bill' posts come down to: a NAT Gateway (hourly + data charges), an idle RDS instance, an Elastic IP not attached to a running instance, or resources in a region you forgot about.
reference_summary: Surprise AWS bill, how do I find what's costing money and stop it. Resolution: Start in Cost Explorer and group by Service, then by Region.

baslik: How do I let an EC2 instance / app access S3 without hardcoding keys?
soru: Right now my app on EC2 has AWS access keys baked into a config file to read from S3, which I know is bad practice. People keep saying use IAM roles instead. How do roles actually work for this and how do I switch without breaking the app?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: Use an IAM Role attached to the EC2 instance (an instance profile). The instance automatically gets temporary, auto-rotating credentials via the instance metadata service, and the AWS SDK picks them up with zero code changes if you remove the hardcoded keys. No secrets on disk, nothing to leak or rotate manually.

Steps: create an IAM Role with a trust policy for ec2.amazonaws.com, attach a policy granting only the S3 actions/buckets the app needs (least privilege, not S3FullAccess), then attach the role to the instance (Actions > Security > Modify IAM Role). The SDK's default credential chain finds it automatically.

Crucially, REMOVE the hardcoded keys from your config and environment. The SDK credential chain checks env vars and config files BEFORE the instance role, so stale hardcoded keys will keep being used (and may be the wrong/over-privileged ones) until you delete them.
For non-EC2 (Lambda, ECS, EKS) the same idea applies via execution roles / IRSA. For local dev use a named profile or SSO, never long-lived keys in code.

Attaching an instance role with a tight S3 policy and deleting the keys from the config worked seamlessly, the SDK transparently used the role's temporary credentials and there's nothing to rotate now.

cozum: Use an IAM Role attached to the EC2 instance (an instance profile). The instance automatically gets temporary, auto-rotating credentials via the instance metadata service, and the AWS SDK picks them up with zero code changes if you remove the hardcoded keys. No secrets on disk, nothing to leak or rotate manually.
reference_summary: How do I let an EC2 instance / app access S3 without hardcoding keys. Resolution: Use an IAM Role attached to the EC2 instance (an instance profile).

baslik: CloudFront serves old content after I update files in S3
soru: I host a static site on S3 behind CloudFront. After I upload new versions of my files to S3, the site keeps showing the old content for hours. I can see the new file directly in the S3 console. How do I make CloudFront serve the updated files immediately?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: CloudFront caches objects at edge locations according to the cache TTL, so after you update the S3 origin, edges keep serving the old cached copy until the TTL expires, that's the 'hours' you're seeing. The new file is in S3, but CloudFront hasn't re-fetched it.

For an immediate update, create an invalidation: CloudFront > your distribution > Invalidations > create one for `/*` (or the specific paths). This purges the edge caches and the next request re-fetches from S3. The first 1,000 invalidation paths per month are free.

Invalidating `/*` on every deploy works but is a blunt instrument. The better long-term pattern is cache-busting: give files content-hashed names (app.3f8a.js) so a new deploy produces new filenames, and the HTML referencing them is the only thing with a short TTL. Then you rarely need invalidations.
Check your cache-control headers on the S3 objects too, set short/zero max-age on index.html and long max-age on hashed assets. That gives instant HTML updates without invalidations.
Adding a `/*` invalidation to my deploy script made updates appear immediately. I later switched to hashed asset filenames so only index.html needs purging.

baslik: Azure App Service returns HTTP 500.30 after deployment
soru: I deployed my .NET app to Azure App Service and the site returns 'HTTP Error 500.30 - ASP.NET Core app failed to start'. It runs fine locally. The deployment succeeded. How do I find out why the app won't start on App Service?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: 500.30 means the app started but crashed during startup, the cause is in your app, and App Service is just reporting the failure. First enable stdout logging or check the logs: in the portal go to your App Service > Log stream, or enable App Service Logs, the real exception (a missing config, a failed DI registration, a bad connection string) will be there.

The most common causes: a connection string or app setting that exists locally (in appsettings.Development.json or user secrets) but isn't set in App Service > Configuration > Application settings. Locally it's present, in Azure it's null and startup throws. Add the missing settings in the portal.
A runtime/version mismatch also does it: the app targets a .NET version the App Service isn't configured for. Check Configuration > General settings > stack and version matches your target framework.

Use the Kudu/SCM console (https://<app>.scm.azurewebsites.net) to see the deployed files and run the app manually, you'll get the raw stack trace immediately, which is far more informative than 500.30.
It was a missing connection string for me, present in local user secrets, absent in Azure config. Adding it under Application settings fixed startup. Log stream showed the exact exception.

First enable stdout logging or check the logs: in the portal go to your App Service > Log stream, or enable App Service Logs, the real exception (a missing config, a failed DI registration, a bad connection string) will be there.

baslik: Azure Blob Storage returns 403 AuthorizationFailure with a SAS token
soru: I generated a SAS token for a blob and my client gets 403 AuthorizationFailure when using it. The token looks correct and I just created it. Reading the same blob from the portal works. What makes a fresh SAS token return 403?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: The top cause is clock/time: a SAS has a start time (st) and expiry (se). If the start time is even slightly in the future relative to Azure's clock, the token isn't valid yet and you get 403. Either omit the start time or set it a few minutes in the past to absorb clock skew.

Second: the permissions and resource type in the SAS don't match the operation. A SAS scoped with read ('r') only will 403 on a write, and a service-level vs container-level vs blob-level SAS grants different scopes. Regenerate with the exact permissions (e.g. 'racwl') and the right signed resource.

If it's an account SAS, check the allowed services/resource types/permissions trio, all three must include what you're doing (e.g. Blob service, Object resource type, Read permission). Missing any one yields 403.

Also confirm you're hitting the right account/container and that there isn't a firewall/network rule on the storage account blocking your IP, network restrictions surface as authorization failures too.
Mine was the start time being in the future due to clock skew. Setting st to 10 minutes earlier (or removing it) made the SAS work immediately.

cozum: The top cause is clock/time: a SAS has a start time (st) and expiry (se). If the start time is even slightly in the future relative to Azure's clock, the token isn't valid yet and you get 403. Either omit the start time or set it a few minutes in the past to absorb clock skew.
reference_summary: Azure Blob Storage returns 403 AuthorizationFailure with a SAS token. Resolution: The top cause is clock/time: a SAS has a start time (st) and expiry (se).

baslik: Can't RDP into my Azure Windows VM, connection fails
soru: My Azure Windows VM is running but I can't connect over RDP, it just fails to connect/times out. I have the right username and password. This worked when I first created the VM. What changed and how do I get back in?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: Like EC2/SSH, an RDP timeout is almost always a Network Security Group rule. Check the NSG on the VM's NIC/subnet allows inbound TCP 3389 from your current IP. If your IP changed (home IPs rotate), the old allow rule no longer matches and you're locked out. Update the source to your current IP.

Use the portal's 'Connection troubleshoot' (under the VM's Help/Networking) or 'Run command' to diagnose without RDP. Run command lets you execute PowerShell on the VM (e.g. to re-enable RDP or check the firewall) even when you can't log in.

If the NSG is fine, the VM's own Windows Firewall or the Remote Desktop service may be off. The portal's 'Reset password' blade can also reset the RDP configuration and the RDP service, a quick fix for a broken RDP stack.

Confirm the VM has a public IP (or you're connecting via Bastion/VPN). If the public IP was disassociated or the VM is in a private subnet, direct RDP won't reach it, use Azure Bastion instead, which is also more secure.
It was the NSG, my home IP had changed. Updating the inbound 3389 rule to 'My IP' restored access. I switched to Bastion afterwards so I stop getting locked out.

cozum: Like EC2/SSH, an RDP timeout is almost always a Network Security Group rule. Check the NSG on the VM's NIC/subnet allows inbound TCP 3389 from your current IP. If your IP changed (home IPs rotate), the old allow rule no longer matches and you're locked out. Update the source to your current IP.
reference_summary: Can't RDP into my Azure Windows VM, connection fails. Resolution: Like EC2/SSH, an RDP timeout is almost always a Network Security Group rule.

baslik: Azure Function is slow on first request (cold start), how to fix?
soru: My Azure Function on the Consumption plan is fast normally but the first request after a period of inactivity takes several seconds. Users hitting it after a quiet spell get a slow response. Is this the famous cold start and what are my realistic options?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: Yes, that's cold start: on the Consumption plan, idle functions are deallocated and the next request must spin up a worker, load the runtime and your dependencies, hence the multi-second first hit. It's inherent to scale-to-zero. Your options trade cost against latency.

Cheapest mitigations first: reduce your dependency/package size and avoid heavy startup work, a leaner function cold-starts faster. For .NET, ReadyToRun/AOT helps; for Node/Python, trim imports and lazy-load. This shaves cold starts without changing plan.

If cold starts are unacceptable, move to the Premium plan, which keeps pre-warmed instances always ready (no scale-to-zero), or the Dedicated/App Service plan where the host is always on. Premium's 'always ready instances' specifically eliminate cold starts.

A common low-cost hack: a timer-triggered 'keep-warm' ping every few minutes so the instance never goes idle. Imperfect (scale-out instances still cold-start) but cheap and good enough for low-traffic apps.
We moved the latency-sensitive function to a Premium plan with one always-ready instance, cold starts disappeared. The keep-warm ping was a fine stopgap before that.

baslik: 401 Unauthorized calling my API protected by Azure AD / Entra ID
soru: My client gets a token from Azure AD (Entra ID) successfully, but when it calls my protected API the API returns 401 Unauthorized. The token looks valid. What are the usual reasons a valid-looking Azure AD token is rejected by the API?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: Decode the token at jwt.ms and check the `aud` (audience) and `iss` (issuer) claims, this resolves most 401s. The API validates that `aud` matches its own Application ID URI / client ID. If your client requested a token for the wrong scope/resource (e.g. Microsoft Graph instead of your API), the aud is wrong and the API rejects it.

Make sure the client requests a scope belonging to YOUR API (api://<your-api-client-id>/access_as_user), not a generic one. A token whose audience is Graph or the client itself will 401 against your API even though acquiring it 'succeeded'.

Check the API's validation config: the expected Authority/tenant, audience, and that it accepts the token version (v1 vs v2 endpoints issue different iss/aud formats). A mismatch between the endpoint your client uses and what the API expects causes 401.
Confirm the token is actually being sent: `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, exact spelling. And that the app registration has the API permission granted with admin consent if required.
It was the audience, my SPA was requesting the default scope and getting a Graph-audience token. Requesting api://.../access_as_user gave a token with the right aud and the 401 cleared.

If your client requested a token for the wrong scope/resource (e.g. Microsoft Graph instead of your API), the aud is wrong and the API rejects it.

baslik: Accidentally left resources running, how do I find and clean up cost in Azure?
soru: I've been experimenting in Azure and now I'm not sure what's still running and costing money. I want to find idle resources and delete what I don't need without nuking something important. What's the systematic way to audit and clean up an Azure subscription?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: Start with Cost Management > Cost analysis, group by Resource and by Resource group. This ranks exactly what's spending. In Azure the usual money pits are: a running VM you forgot, a Premium/Standard managed disk left after deleting a VM, public IPs, a NAT Gateway, App Service plans (you pay for the plan even with no apps), and Log Analytics ingestion.

Use 'Advisor' (Cost recommendations) which flags idle and underutilized resources (VMs with low CPU, unattached disks, idle public IPs) and even estimates the savings. It's the fastest way to find safe-to-delete waste.

Organize by resource group: if you created throwaway experiments in their own resource groups, you can delete the whole group at once, which removes every resource in it cleanly. Keep production in clearly named groups so you never delete the wrong one.

Watch for orphans after deleting a VM: the OS/data disks, NICs, and public IPs often survive and keep billing. Filter the resource list by type (Disks, Public IP addresses) and delete unattached ones.

Cost analysis grouped by resource group plus Advisor's idle-resource list let me delete a forgotten VM, two unattached disks and an idle App Service plan. Set a budget alert so it won't creep up again.

baslik: VLOOKUP returns #N/A even though the value clearly exists
soru: My VLOOKUP keeps returning #N/A but I can see the lookup value in the other table with my own eyes. The formula syntax looks right. This is driving me crazy, the value is definitely there. What invisible thing causes VLOOKUP to not find a value that exists?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: 99% of the time it's a hidden mismatch you can't see: leading/trailing spaces, or one side is a number-stored-as-text while the other is a real number. '12345 ' with a trailing space, or text '12345' vs numeric 12345, will never match even though they look identical on screen.

Test it: in a blank cell do `=A2=D2` comparing the two values, if it returns FALSE they're not actually equal. Use `=TRIM(A2)` to strip spaces, and `=ISNUMBER(A2)` on each to check whether one is text and the other numeric. Fixing the type/space mismatch fixes the #N/A.

Second classic cause: VLOOKUP's 4th argument. If you omit it or use TRUE, it does an approximate match and needs the lookup column sorted. For exact matching always use `VLOOKUP(x, range, col, FALSE)` (or 0). Leaving it off on unsorted data returns #N/A or wrong values.

Also confirm the lookup value is in the FIRST column of your table_array, VLOOKUP only searches the leftmost column. If your ID is in column B of the range, VLOOKUP can't find it. Use INDEX/MATCH or XLOOKUP, which don't have that restriction.

Mine was numbers stored as text on one sheet. Multiplying that column by 1 (or Text to Columns > Finish to coerce) made them real numbers and VLOOKUP matched instantly. XLOOKUP is worth switching to anyway.

baslik: Excel warns about a circular reference and my formulas show 0
soru: Excel popped up a 'circular reference' warning and now some of my cells show 0 or wrong totals. I didn't intentionally create a loop. How do I find the circular reference and fix it, the warning isn't telling me where it is clearly?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: A circular reference means a formula refers back to its own cell, directly or through a chain (A depends on B depends on A). Excel can't resolve it so it shows 0 or stops calculating. The fix is finding the loop, and Excel will point you to it.

Go to Formulas tab > Error Checking dropdown > Circular References. It lists the exact cells in the loop. Click one to jump there. Usually it's a SUM that accidentally includes its own cell, e.g. =SUM(B1:B10) sitting in B10, so the total includes itself.

The status bar at the bottom also shows 'Circular References: B10' telling you the offending cell. Trace Precedents (Formulas > Trace Precedents) draws arrows showing what feeds the cell, which makes the loop visible.
Once found, fix the range so it excludes the formula's own cell (=SUM(B1:B9) if the total is in B10), or restructure so the dependency only goes one direction.

If you actually WANT iterative calculation (rare, e.g. some engineering models), enable it in File > Options > Formulas > Enable iterative calculation, but for a normal spreadsheet you want to remove the loop, not enable iteration.
It was a self-including SUM, the total cell was inside its own summed range. Trimming the range to exclude that cell cleared the warning and the totals were correct.

cozum: A circular reference means a formula refers back to its own cell, directly or through a chain (A depends on B depends on A). Excel can't resolve it so it shows 0 or stops calculating. The fix is finding the loop, and Excel will point you to it.
reference_summary: Excel warns about a circular reference and my formulas show 0. Resolution: A circular reference means a formula refers back to its own cell, directly or through a chain (A depends on B depends on A).

baslik: Dates imported as text won't sort or work in formulas
soru: I imported data and the dates are left-aligned and treated as text, so they won't sort chronologically and date functions return errors. They look like dates (e.g. 15/03/2024) but Excel won't treat them as real dates. How do I convert a whole column of text dates into real dates?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: Text dates are left-aligned (real dates are right-aligned by default), and that's your tell. The cleanest bulk fix is Data > Text to Columns: select the column, Text to Columns > Delimited > Next > Next, then on step 3 choose 'Date' and pick the format matching your data (e.g. DMY for 15/03/2024), Finish. The whole column converts to real dates instantly.

Text to Columns is the go-to because it correctly interprets the day/month order, which matters for DD/MM vs MM/DD data. Choosing the wrong order silently swaps days and months, so pick DMY or MDY to match the source.

Alternatively use a helper column with DATEVALUE: `=DATEVALUE(A2)` turns the text into a date serial number, then format the result as a date and paste-special values back. DATEVALUE respects your regional settings, so confirm the order is interpreted correctly.

If the text format is unusual, build the date explicitly: `=DATE(RIGHT(A2,4), MID(A2,4,2), LEFT(A2,2))` for dd/mm/yyyy text. Bulletproof regardless of locale because you control which substring is day/month/year.
Text to Columns with the DMY option converted my entire column to genuine dates that sort and feed date functions correctly. It was the fastest path for a few thousand rows.

cozum: Text dates are left-aligned (real dates are right-aligned by default), and that's your tell. The cleanest bulk fix is Data > Text to Columns: select the column, Text to Columns > Delimited > Next > Next, then on step 3 choose 'Date' and pick the format matching your data (e.g. DMY for 15/03/2024), Finish. The whole column converts to real dates instantly.

baslik: Excel file is huge and painfully slow to open and edit
soru: My workbook has grown to like 40MB and takes ages to open, and every edit lags as it recalculates. It's mostly formulas and some data. What makes Excel files balloon and slow down, and how do I make it fast again without losing my work?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: The two biggest causes of bloat and slowness are: (1) formulas referencing entire columns (e.g. =SUMIF(A:A,...)) which force Excel to evaluate a million rows each time, and (2) volatile functions (NOW, TODAY, OFFSET, INDIRECT, RAND) that recalculate on every change. Both make every edit recompute huge ranges.

Fix the ranges first: replace whole-column references with the actual used range (A2:A5000 instead of A:A). This alone often turns a laggy file snappy. Excel Tables (Ctrl+T) with structured references auto-size to your data and avoid the whole-column trap.

Find phantom bloat: press Ctrl+End. If it jumps far below/right of your real data, you have millions of empty-but-formatted cells inflating the file. Delete those entire rows/columns, save, and the file shrinks dramatically.

Replace heavy array/volatile formulas where possible, convert finished calculations to static values (Paste Special > Values) for data that no longer changes, and set Calculation to Manual (Formulas > Calculation Options) while editing, then F9 to recalc on demand.
Trimming whole-column SUMIFs to real ranges and deleting a huge block of formatted-but-empty cells (Ctrl+End revealed row 1,000,000) cut my file from 40MB to 6MB and made it instant.

baslik: Formulas suddenly show #REF! after I deleted some rows/columns
soru: I deleted a few columns I thought were unused, and now a bunch of formulas elsewhere show #REF! errors. I can undo, but I want to understand what happened and how to fix the formulas without rebuilding everything. What does #REF! mean here?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: #REF! means a formula is pointing at a cell/range that no longer exists, you deleted a column or row that some formula referenced, so its reference is now invalid and Excel replaces it with #REF!. The formula structure survives but the broken reference is literally written into it (e.g. =A2+#REF!).

If you just did the deletion, the cleanest fix is Ctrl+Z to undo, then before deleting, use Formulas > Trace Dependents on the columns to see what relies on them. Anything with dependents shouldn't be deleted blindly.

If you can't undo, find all the errors fast: Home > Find & Select > Go To Special > Formulas > Errors selects every error cell. Or Ctrl+F and search for '#REF!' within formulas (Look in: Formulas). Then repair each by re-pointing it at the correct surviving cell.

To repair in bulk where the pattern is consistent, Find & Replace can swap '#REF!' for the correct reference if they all should point to the same place, otherwise fix them individually using the traced logic.

I undid, then used Trace Dependents and discovered the 'unused' column fed three summary formulas. I moved those calculations first, then deleted safely. Go To Special > Errors is great for hunting any that slipped through.

cozum: #REF! means a formula is pointing at a cell/range that no longer exists, you deleted a column or row that some formula referenced, so its reference is now invalid and Excel replaces it with #REF!. baslik: 'File is locked for editing by another user' but no one has it open
soru: Our shared Excel file on the network/OneDrive says it's 'locked for editing by another user' or opens read-only, but nobody actually has it open. We can't edit it. How do I clear the phantom lock and prevent it happening?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: A phantom lock usually means a previous session didn't close cleanly, Excel leaves a hidden owner/lock file (e.g. ~$Filename.xlsx) next to the document, and until that's removed Excel thinks someone still has it open. Close Excel on all machines, then delete the hidden ~$ file in the same folder (enable 'show hidden files' to see it).

On a network share, a crashed client or a stale SMB session can hold the lock. If deleting the ~$ file isn't enough, the file server admin can clear the open-file handle (Computer Management > Shared Folders > Open Files) which releases it.

For OneDrive/SharePoint, the lock is server-side: someone (or a sync conflict) may hold it. Use the web version (Open in browser) which uses co-authoring instead of exclusive locks, or wait a few minutes for the server lock to time out. AutoSave + co-authoring avoids exclusive locks entirely.
To prevent recurrence on a heavily shared file, move it to SharePoint/OneDrive and use co-authoring so multiple people edit simultaneously, rather than the old exclusive-lock model on a file share.
Deleting the leftover ~$ owner file in the folder cleared the phantom lock for us. We later moved the workbook to SharePoint so co-authoring replaced the locking entirely.

baslik: Email stuck in Outbox and won't send
soru: I have an email sitting in my Outlook Outbox that won't send, it just stays there. New emails queue up behind it. I'm connected to the internet and can receive mail fine. How do I get the stuck message to send or at least clear it so the others go?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: The most common cause is a large attachment exceeding the server's size limit, the message can't upload so it jams the Outbox and blocks everything behind it. Open the stuck message (you may need to switch to Offline mode first, Send/Receive > Work Offline, so Outlook stops trying to send it while you edit), and either remove/shrink the attachment or delete the message.

If you can't open it because Outlook keeps trying to send, go offline (Work Offline), then drag the stuck message from Outbox to Drafts. Now it's not being transmitted and you can edit or delete it safely, then go back online.

Sometimes it's an authentication hiccup, the send fails silently and retries forever. Restart Outlook, and check File > Account Settings that your account isn't prompting for a password. Re-entering credentials often releases the queue.
Check the message isn't set to send at a future time (Options > Delay Delivery) and that your Send/Receive isn't paused. Press F9 (Send/Receive All) once it's online and unblocked.
Mine was a 30MB attachment over the server limit. Going offline, moving the message to Drafts, and sending the file via a OneDrive link instead cleared the Outbox and the queued emails went out.

baslik: Outlook not receiving new emails but webmail shows them
soru: New emails show up when I check my account in the browser, but Outlook on my desktop doesn't pull them in, or does so hours late. Send works. I've checked I'm online. How do I get Outlook to sync new mail reliably again?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: First rule out Work Offline being toggled on, it's easy to hit accidentally. Send/Receive tab > check the 'Work Offline' button isn't highlighted. If it is, click it to go back online. This is the number one cause of 'Outlook stopped getting mail'.

Force a sync with F9 (Send/Receive All Folders). If that pulls the mail, your automatic send/receive interval may be off or too long, check Send/Receive > Send/Receive Groups > Define Send/Receive Groups and ensure 'Schedule an automatic send/receive every X minutes' is enabled.

A bloated or corrupted local data file (.ost/.pst) commonly causes sync to stall. For an Exchange/Microsoft 365 account, closing Outlook and renaming/deleting the .ost forces Outlook to rebuild it from the server cleanly (your mail is safe on the server). For POP/PST, run scanpst.exe to repair the file.
Check you're not over the mailbox or local file size limit, and that no rule is moving incoming mail to another folder so it just looks like nothing arrived. Look in all folders / search to be sure.
It was a corrupted OST. Closing Outlook and letting it rebuild the OST from the server restored real-time sync. F9 is my reflex now if it ever lags.

baslik: Outlook keeps asking for my password over and over
soru: Outlook repeatedly pops up the password prompt for my Microsoft 365 account. I type the correct password, it accepts it, then a minute later asks again. It's relentless. How do I stop the endless password prompts?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: For a Microsoft 365/Exchange account this is usually a stale cached credential conflicting with modern authentication. Close Outlook, open Windows Credential Manager (Control Panel > Credential Manager > Windows Credentials), and delete every entry mentioning Outlook/Office/MicrosoftOffice. Reopen Outlook and sign in once, fresh, it stops re-prompting.

Make sure modern authentication is being used and the account is added as a proper Microsoft 365 account, not a legacy manual IMAP/Exchange setup. Removing and re-adding the account via File > Add Account (letting it auto-configure) often resolves repeated prompts.

If your organization uses MFA/conditional access, an expired token or a device that fell out of compliance triggers constant prompts. Signing out and back in (or completing the MFA prompt fully) re-establishes the token.
Also check the 'Remember my credentials' box is ticked when you sign in, and that Outlook is fully updated, an old build with deprecated auth can loop on prompts against modern 365.
Clearing the Office entries in Credential Manager and signing in once cleanly stopped the loop for me. It was a corrupted cached token.

baslik: Outlook search returns no results or misses recent emails
soru: Outlook's search either returns nothing or clearly misses emails I know exist (I can see them by scrolling). It's like the index is broken. How do I rebuild Outlook's search so it finds everything again?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: This is a search index problem, Windows Search indexes Outlook, and when the index is incomplete or corrupted, searches miss mail that's plainly there. The fix is to rebuild the index. Go to File > Options > Search > Indexing Options > Advanced > Rebuild. It takes a while to re-index but restores complete results.

First check what's being indexed: Search Options > 'Indexing Options' and confirm Microsoft Outlook is in the list of indexed locations. If Outlook isn't listed, search can't work properly, add it, then rebuild.
A quick tell: if searching shows 'indexing is in progress' or results trickle in, just let it finish, a recent large mailbox or a just-rebuilt OST needs time to index fully before search is complete.

If rebuilding doesn't help, the OST/PST may be the issue, repair it (scanpst.exe for PST) or rebuild the OST. Also ensure Windows Search service is running (services.msc > Windows Search > Running/Automatic); if that service is stopped, Outlook search fails entirely.
Rebuilding the index via Indexing Options > Advanced fixed it, after it finished re-indexing, search found everything including the recent mail it had been missing.

baslik: Meeting invites disappear or don't show up properly on the calendar
soru: When I accept a meeting invite, it sometimes doesn't appear on my calendar, or invites vanish from the inbox before I can respond. Colleagues say I'm not showing as accepted. What's mishandling my calendar invites and how do I fix it?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: A very common cause is the 'automatically process meeting requests' setting combined with a rogue rule or an add-in. First check File > Options > Mail > 'Automatically process meeting requests and responses to meeting requests and polls', if this is on, Outlook may auto-file invites before you see them. Toggle it to match your expectation.

Check for Inbox rules that move or delete messages, a rule catching meeting-invite emails will whisk them away before you respond, making it look like they vanished and you never accepted. Rules > Manage Rules & Alerts and review anything touching meeting items.

If invites are accepted but don't land on the calendar, a corrupted OST or a delegate/permission misconfiguration is likely. Rebuilding the OST (close Outlook, let it recreate from the server) restores proper calendar processing.

Make sure you don't have multiple calendars and are looking at the wrong one, and that the account receiving invites is the one whose calendar you're viewing. Also try the web calendar (OWA) to confirm whether the issue is the desktop client or the mailbox itself.
A leftover Inbox rule was deleting invites that matched a subject pattern. Removing the rule plus rebuilding the OST fixed both the disappearing invites and the calendar not updating.

baslik: Outlook blocks certain attachments, 'Outlook blocked access to unsafe attachments'
soru: Someone sent me a file and Outlook says 'Outlook blocked access to the following potentially unsafe attachments' and I can't open or save it. It's a legitimate file I need. How do I get the blocked attachment without disabling all security?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: Outlook hard-blocks a list of 'Level 1' file types (.exe, .bat, .js, .vbs and others) because they're common malware vectors, you can't open or save them from within Outlook at all. The safe and easy fix is to ask the sender to re-send it inside a .zip; Outlook doesn't block zip contents, and you extract the file after scanning it.

Other safe options: have the sender share it via OneDrive/SharePoint/Google Drive as a link, or rename the extension before sending (e.g. file.exe to file.ex_) and you rename it back after saving. These avoid touching Outlook's security at all.

If you genuinely must un-block a type and understand the risk (admin/IT context), it's a registry change (Level1Remove under the Outlook Security key) that removes a specific extension from the blocked list. Only do this deliberately and re-block afterward, it lowers protection for everyone using that profile.
Before opening any previously-blocked file, scan it with your antivirus, the block exists precisely because these types are dangerous. Verify the sender actually meant to send an executable.
We just had the sender zip the file, Outlook let the .zip through, and I extracted the file after an AV scan. No need to weaken Outlook's settings.

baslik: Chrome using huge amounts of RAM and slowing my computer
soru: Chrome is eating gigabytes of RAM, my whole computer slows down and the fan spins up. I have a fair number of tabs open but nothing crazy. Why is Chrome so memory-hungry and what can I actually do to reduce it without closing everything?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: Each tab and extension runs as its own process (for security and stability), so memory adds up fast, and extensions are often the worst offenders, not the tabs. Open Chrome's own Task Manager (Shift+Esc or Menu > More tools > Task Manager) to see exactly which tabs and extensions use the most memory. You'll often find one extension or one heavy site is the real hog.

Enable the built-in Memory Saver: Settings > Performance > Memory Saver. It puts inactive tabs to sleep and frees their memory, reloading them when you click back. This dramatically cuts RAM use for people who keep many tabs open.
Audit extensions, disable ones you don't use (chrome://extensions). Some extensions inject scripts into every page and leak memory over time. Disabling a couple often reclaims a surprising amount.

Heavy sites (web apps, lots of media, ad-laden pages) keep their tab process large. The Task Manager pinpoints them; close or suspend the worst, and consider an ad blocker which reduces per-page memory.
Chrome's Task Manager revealed one extension using 1.5GB. Removing it plus turning on Memory Saver cut Chrome's footprint by more than half and the fan settled down.

cozum: Each tab and extension runs as its own process (for security and stability), so memory adds up fast, and extensions are often the worst offenders, not the tabs. Open Chrome's own Task Manager (Shift+Esc or Menu > More tools > Task Manager) to see exactly which tabs and extensions use the most memory. You'll often find one extension or one heavy site is the real hog.
reference_summary: Chrome using huge amounts of RAM and slowing my computer. Resolution: Each tab and extension runs as its own process (for security and stability), so memory adds up fast, and extensions are often the worst offenders, not the tabs.

baslik: ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID / 'Your connection is not private' on sites that should be fine
soru: Chrome shows 'Your connection is not private' (NET::ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID) on lots of normally-trusted sites, even big ones. It can't all be the sites' fault. What on my end causes Chrome to reject valid certificates and how do I fix it?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: When it happens on MANY trusted sites at once, the cause is almost always your computer's clock being wrong. TLS certificate validation checks the cert's valid date range against your system time, if your clock is days off, every cert looks expired or not-yet-valid. Fix the date/time (set it to automatic/network time) and the errors vanish.

Set Windows/Mac to sync time automatically: Windows Settings > Time & language > set time automatically and 'Sync now'; macOS System Settings > General > Date & Time > set automatically. A drained CMOS battery or a bad timezone is the usual reason it drifted.

If the clock is correct and it's still many sites, suspect antivirus/firewall HTTPS scanning or a corporate proxy intercepting TLS with a root the system doesn't trust, exactly like the corporate-CA case. Temporarily disable AV HTTPS scanning to test.
For a single site only, then it really is that site's expired cert and you should wait for them to renew, not bypass it. The mass-failure pattern is what points at your clock.
It was my clock, the laptop's CMOS battery died and the date reset to 2010. Enabling automatic time sync fixed certificate errors across every site at once.

baslik: Chrome stopped offering to save passwords
soru: Chrome used to offer to save my passwords and now it just doesn't ask anymore, even on new sites. I have to type everything manually. I haven't changed settings on purpose. How do I get the save-password prompt back?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: First check the setting is still on: chrome://settings/passwords (or Settings > Autofill > Password Manager > Settings) and make sure 'Offer to save passwords' is enabled. It can get switched off by a profile sync glitch or an update.

Check the site isn't on the 'Never saved' list, if you once clicked 'Never' for a site, Chrome won't ask again for it. In Password Manager settings scroll to 'Never saved' and remove entries you want prompts for.

If you're in Incognito or a Guest profile, Chrome deliberately won't save passwords, make sure you're in your normal profile. Also confirm you're signed into Chrome and sync is working, a broken sync can suppress prompts.
An extension (some password managers) can take over and suppress Chrome's own prompt, that's expected if you use LastPass/1Password etc. If you don't intend that, disable the conflicting extension.
Mine was the 'Offer to save passwords' toggle, an update had flipped it off. Re-enabling it brought the prompts back. I also cleared one site from the 'Never saved' list.

baslik: 'Page Unresponsive' messages keep appearing
soru: I keep getting 'Page Unresponsive - you can wait or exit' popups in Chrome, on various sites. Sometimes waiting recovers, sometimes I have to kill the tab. It's frequent enough to be annoying. What causes this and how do I reduce it?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: 'Page Unresponsive' means that tab's process stopped responding, usually the page's JavaScript is stuck in a loop or the tab ran out of memory. If it's many different sites, the cause is more likely your environment (an extension, low memory, hardware acceleration) than the sites.

Test in Incognito (extensions are off by default there). If the problem disappears, an extension is the culprit, re-enable them one at a time to find which. Misbehaving extensions are the most common cause of widespread unresponsiveness.

Toggle hardware acceleration: Settings > System > 'Use graphics acceleration when available'. On some GPUs/drivers this causes hangs, turning it off (or on, if it was off) and restarting Chrome resolves a lot of these freezes.

Clear cache and update Chrome and your graphics driver. Low RAM also triggers it, close other heavy apps and enable Memory Saver. If one specific site always does it, that page has a script bug, not much you can do beyond reporting it.
Disabling hardware acceleration fixed the constant 'Page Unresponsive' popups for me, it was a driver issue with my GPU. Updating the GPU driver later let me turn acceleration back on.

baslik: Chrome blocks downloads: 'file can't be downloaded securely' or 'blocked'
soru: Chrome refuses to let me download certain files, saying things like 'can't be downloaded securely' or it's 'blocked', even for files I trust. How do I download a file Chrome is blocking, when I'm confident it's safe?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: The 'can't be downloaded securely' message appears when a file is served over insecure HTTP from an otherwise HTTPS page (mixed content), Chrome blocks it to prevent tampering. If you trust the source, click the blocked download in the downloads bar/list, there's usually a 'Keep' option to override.

For files flagged as dangerous, go to chrome://downloads, find the blocked item and click 'Keep' / 'Keep dangerous file' to force it. Only do this when you genuinely trust the file, the warning is Safe Browsing protecting you from malware.

If Safe Browsing 'Enhanced protection' is too aggressive for your workflow, Settings > Privacy and security > Security lets you switch to 'Standard protection', which blocks fewer downloads. Don't disable it entirely.
Mixed-content blocks are fixed properly by the site serving the file over HTTPS. As a user, the 'Keep' override is your tool, but verify the URL is the real source first.
Clicking 'Keep' in chrome://downloads let me save the file. It was a mixed-content block (HTTP file on an HTTPS page); the source was legitimate so the override was safe.

baslik: 'Your profile could not be opened correctly' on Chrome startup
soru: Every time I start Chrome I get 'Your profile could not be opened correctly. Some features may be unavailable.' My bookmarks and extensions seem intact but the message is annoying and sometimes things don't sync. How do I fix the corrupted profile?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: This means a file in your Chrome profile got corrupted, often the 'Web Data' or 'Preferences' file, usually from an unclean shutdown or disk issue. The targeted fix: close Chrome, open your profile folder, and rename/delete the corrupted file (commonly 'Web Data'); Chrome rebuilds it on next launch. Your bookmarks and passwords live in separate files and are unaffected.

Profile folder location: Windows %LOCALAPPDATA%\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default, Mac ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/Default. Close Chrome fully first (check it's not in the tray), then rename 'Web Data' to 'Web Data.old' and restart.

If that doesn't clear it, create a fresh profile: chrome://settings > you and Google > add a new profile, sign in, and your synced data (bookmarks, passwords, extensions) flows back from your Google account. Then you can delete the broken profile.
Run a quick disk check too, repeated profile corruption can indicate a failing drive or aggressive antivirus locking Chrome's files during write.
Renaming the 'Web Data' file in the Default profile folder fixed the startup error, Chrome rebuilt it cleanly and the message never came back. Nothing was lost.

baslik: VS Code can't find my Python interpreter / imports show as unresolved
soru: In VS Code my Python code runs but every import is underlined as 'unresolved' / 'could not be resolved', and IntelliSense doesn't work for installed packages. The packages ARE installed (the code runs in the terminal). How do I point VS Code at the right Python so it stops flagging imports?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: VS Code's analysis (Pylance) uses the selected interpreter, which may differ from the one your terminal uses. If they differ, the editor looks in the wrong site-packages and can't find your installed packages, hence 'unresolved' even though it runs. Fix: click the Python version in the bottom-right status bar (or Ctrl+Shift+P > 'Python: Select Interpreter') and choose the interpreter/venv where your packages are installed.
If you use a virtual environment, select the venv's python explicitly (./venv/bin/python). Once Pylance points at the venv, the unresolved-import squiggles disappear and IntelliSense works.
After switching, reload the window (Ctrl+Shift+P > 'Developer: Reload Window') so the language server re-scans with the new interpreter. Sometimes the squiggles linger until a reload.
Confirm with 'Python: Select Interpreter' that the chosen path matches `which python` in the terminal where imports work. When they match, the editor and runtime agree.
Selecting my project's venv as the interpreter and reloading the window cleared every unresolved-import error instantly, VS Code had defaulted to the system Python which didn't have my packages.

baslik: My code changes don't take effect, like VS Code isn't saving
soru: I edit a file, run it, and my changes don't seem to take effect, the old behavior persists. It's like VS Code isn't saving or it's running an old version. I do see my edits in the editor. What's going on and how do I make sure I'm running what I see?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: First, the dot on the tab: an unsaved file shows a filled dot instead of an X on its tab. If you run without saving, you run the last saved version, not what's on screen. Save (Ctrl+S) before running, or enable Files: Auto Save (File > Auto Save) so this can't happen.

If you ARE saving and still get old behavior, you're probably running a different file or a stale build/cache. Check the run configuration / which file the run button targets, and for compiled languages make sure you rebuild (the run task may be executing an old binary).
For Python, a leftover __pycache__ or running a different copy of the file (wrong working directory) causes this. Confirm the integrated terminal's path and that you're executing the file you edited.

Watch for two copies of the project open, or editing a file in one folder while running from another (common with symlinks or duplicated clones). The path in the terminal vs the file's path should match.
It was unsaved changes, I'd disabled auto-save and kept running the stale saved version. Turning on Auto Save fixed it permanently.

baslik: VS Code is slow / high CPU, suspect an extension
soru: VS Code has become sluggish, typing lags and the CPU spikes. I have a bunch of extensions installed. How do I figure out which extension is slowing it down without uninstalling them one by one blindly?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: VS Code has a built-in tool for exactly this. Run Ctrl+Shift+P > 'Developer: Show Running Extensions', it lists each extension with its activation time and CPU usage, and flags any that are slow. The offender usually stands out with a high activation or 'unresponsive' time.

There's also 'Developer: Startup Performance' which breaks down what's slow at launch. And you can run `code --disable-extensions` to start a clean session, if it's snappy, an extension is definitely the cause and you've confirmed it before hunting.

To bisect quickly, use Extension Bisect: Ctrl+Shift+P > 'Help: Start Extension Bisect'. It automatically disables half your extensions, you say whether it's better, and it narrows down to the culprit in a few rounds, far faster than one-by-one.

Common heavy extensions: large language servers, real-time linters scanning the whole repo, and Git extensions on huge repos. Once identified, you can configure it to be less aggressive rather than removing it.
'Show Running Extensions' immediately pointed at a linter extension pegging CPU on save. Configuring it to lint on-demand instead of on every keystroke fixed the lag.

baslik: Command works in my normal terminal but 'command not found' in VS Code's integrated terminal
soru: A CLI tool (node, python, a custom command) runs fine in my regular terminal app, but in VS Code's integrated terminal I get 'command not found'. Same machine, same user. Why does the integrated terminal have a different environment and how do I fix it?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: The integrated terminal may launch a different shell or not load the same profile files, so your PATH additions (from .zshrc/.bash_profile, nvm, pyenv, etc.) aren't applied. Check which shell each uses: run `echo $SHELL` and `echo $0` in both. If VS Code uses bash while your tool's PATH is set in .zshrc, it won't be found.

Set VS Code's default shell to match your normal one: Ctrl+Shift+P > 'Terminal: Select Default Profile' and pick zsh (or whatever your main terminal uses). New terminals then load the same profile and PATH.

Login vs non-login shell matters: tools like nvm/pyenv often hook in via .bash_profile/.zprofile (login shells) but VS Code may start a non-login interactive shell that only reads .bashrc/.zshrc. Move the PATH setup to the file the interactive shell reads, or configure the terminal profile with `args: ['-l']` to force a login shell.

If VS Code was launched from the GUI (Dock/Start menu) rather than from a terminal, it may not inherit your shell's environment at all. Launching VS Code by typing `code .` from your configured terminal makes it inherit the full environment.
Setting the default profile to zsh (matching my normal terminal) and ensuring nvm's init was in .zshrc made node resolve in the integrated terminal. It had been starting a bare bash without my PATH.

baslik: VS Code says 'Git not found' even though git is installed
soru: VS Code's Source Control panel says 'Git not found. Install it or configure it using the git.path setting.' But I have git installed, I use it in the terminal constantly. How do I make VS Code find my git?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: VS Code looks for git on the PATH it was launched with, which (especially when launched from the GUI) may not include the directory where git lives. Confirm git's location with `which git` (or `where git` on Windows), then set it explicitly: Settings > search 'git.path' and put the full path to the git executable.

On Windows the usual fix is installing Git for Windows and choosing the option to add git to PATH during setup, then restart VS Code so it picks up the updated PATH. If git was installed without PATH integration, VS Code can't see it.

If you launched VS Code from the Start menu/Dock, it may have a stale environment. Fully quit VS Code and relaunch, ideally by running `code .` from a terminal where git works, so it inherits that PATH.

Set `git.path` in settings.json to the absolute path as a guaranteed fix, e.g. on Windows "C:\\Program Files\\Git\\bin\\git.exe", on Mac "/usr/bin/git" or the Homebrew path. This bypasses PATH discovery entirely.
Setting git.path to the absolute path from `which git` made the Source Control panel work immediately, VS Code had been launched without that directory on its PATH.

baslik: Raspberry Pi won't boot, just a red light, no green blinking
soru: My Raspberry Pi won't boot. The red power LED is on solid but the green activity LED never blinks, and nothing appears on the monitor. It worked yesterday. What does 'red on, green silent' mean and how do I get it booting again?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: Red solid + no green activity means the Pi has power but isn't reading the SD card, the green LED blinks when it accesses the card during boot. So the cause is almost always the SD card (corrupted, unseated, or dead) or a missing/corrupt boot partition. Reseat the card first, then suspect the card itself.

Corrupted SD cards are the #1 Pi failure, they wear out from constant writes and don't survive abrupt power-offs well. Put the card in another computer: if it's unreadable or the boot partition is gone, re-flash Raspberry Pi OS with Raspberry Pi Imager onto the same or a new card.
Rule out power: an underpowered supply causes flaky boots and the rainbow screen. Use the official supply or a known 5V/3A USB-C (Pi 4) source. A weak phone charger often can't boot a Pi reliably.

If a freshly flashed card still won't boot, test with the monitor connected before powering on (HDMI must be plugged in at boot), and try without any HATs/USB devices attached in case something is drawing too much current.
It was a corrupted SD card from a power-cut. Re-flashing Raspberry Pi OS onto a new card brought it straight back. I now use a UPS-style supply and back up the card image.

baslik: Raspberry Pi keeps losing WiFi connection
soru: My headless Pi keeps dropping off the WiFi, I lose SSH access and have to power-cycle it. It reconnects for a while then drops again. The router is close by and other devices are stable. How do I stop the Pi's WiFi from dropping?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: The most common cause is WiFi power management, the Pi puts the wireless adapter to sleep to save power, which drops idle connections (exactly what kills a headless SSH session). Disable it: `sudo iw dev wlan0 set power_save off`, and make it permanent so it survives reboots. This fixes the majority of Pi WiFi-drop cases.
To make it stick, add the power_save off command to a startup script or a NetworkManager/dhcpcd hook, otherwise it resets on reboot. Many people drop it in /etc/rc.local or a systemd service.

Underpowered supply also causes WiFi instability, when the Pi browns out under load the radio is the first thing to misbehave. Use the official 5V/3A supply and check for the under-voltage lightning-bolt warning in `vcgencmd get_throttled` (non-zero means power problems).
If you're far from the router or on a crowded 2.4GHz band, try a fixed channel or a small USB WiFi dongle with a better antenna. The Pi's onboard antenna is modest.
Disabling WiFi power_save was the fix, my headless Pi had been sleeping its radio during idle SSH. After turning it off permanently it's stayed connected for weeks.

baslik: Can't SSH into a fresh Raspberry Pi, connection refused
soru: I flashed Raspberry Pi OS and want to run it headless, but SSH gives 'connection refused'. I know the Pi's IP. On older guides SSH just worked. What changed and how do I enable SSH on a headless Pi without a monitor?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: Two things changed in recent Raspberry Pi OS: SSH is disabled by default, and there's no default 'pi/raspberry' user anymore, you must create a user. 'Connection refused' means the SSH server isn't running because it wasn't enabled. The clean fix is to set this up when flashing.

Use Raspberry Pi Imager's settings (the gear/Ctrl+Shift+X before writing): there you enable SSH, set the username and password, and configure WiFi. Flashing with those options means SSH is on and a user exists from first boot, no monitor needed.

If the card's already flashed, mount the boot partition on your computer and create an empty file named `ssh` (no extension) in it, that enables the SSH server on next boot. For the user, add a `userconf.txt` file with the username and an encrypted password (the Imager method is easier).

Confirm the Pi is actually on the network and you have the right IP (check your router's client list). 'Connection refused' is SSH not running; a wrong IP would give 'timeout' or 'no route' instead, useful to distinguish.
Re-flashing with Raspberry Pi Imager and enabling SSH + setting a user in its advanced settings was the simplest fix, the Pi came up headless with SSH ready on first boot.

baslik: Lightning bolt icon and random freezes / slowdowns on my Pi
soru: I see a little lightning bolt icon in the top corner of my Pi's screen and it sometimes freezes or runs slowly, especially when I plug in a USB drive. Is this a power problem and how do I confirm and fix it?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: Yes, the lightning bolt is the under-voltage warning, the Pi detected its supply dropped below ~4.63V. It then throttles the CPU (causing slowdowns) and can freeze or corrupt the SD card. It's the single most common cause of mysterious Pi instability, and it's a power problem, not a software one.

Confirm it with `vcgencmd get_throttled`. A result of 0x0 is fine; any non-zero value indicates under-voltage has occurred (bit 0 = currently under-voltage, bit 16 = has happened since boot). This tells you definitively it's power.

Fix: use the official Raspberry Pi USB-C supply (5V/3A for Pi 4, 5V/5A for Pi 5) and a good quality cable, thin or long cables drop voltage. Phone chargers and PC USB ports usually can't supply enough, especially once you add a USB drive.
Power-hungry USB peripherals (spinning hard drives, some SSDs) can exceed what the Pi can supply, use a powered USB hub for those so they don't draw from the Pi's rail and trigger brownouts.
It was the cable and charger, a cheap USB-C cable was dropping voltage under load. The official supply made the lightning bolt and the freezes disappear, and get_throttled now reads 0x0.

baslik: SD card keeps getting corrupted on my Raspberry Pi
soru: This is the second SD card that's become corrupted in my Pi, the filesystem breaks and it won't boot. I shut it down properly most of the time. What causes repeated SD corruption and how do I make my Pi setup more reliable?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: Repeated SD corruption usually comes from a combination of: abrupt power loss (even occasional), under-voltage (see the lightning-bolt check), cheap/counterfeit SD cards, and heavy write activity wearing the card out. Pulling power without a clean shutdown mid-write is the biggest killer, the filesystem is left inconsistent.

Use a good-quality card from a reputable brand (counterfeits with fake capacity are rampant and fail fast), and verify it with h2testw or f3 to confirm it's genuine. A real, decent endurance card lasts far longer than a no-name one.

Reduce writes: move logs to RAM (log2ram), disable swap or move it off the card, and avoid databases doing constant small writes on the SD. For write-heavy projects, boot from a USB SSD instead of an SD card, the Pi 4/5 support USB boot and SSDs are vastly more durable.

Always shut down cleanly (`sudo shutdown -h now`) and fix any power issues, an under-volting supply both throttles and corrupts. A small UPS or a supply with a clean cutoff prevents the abrupt-power-loss corruption.
Switching to USB-SSD boot plus log2ram and a proper power supply ended the corruption for me, the SD card had simply been wearing out under constant log writes and the odd power cut finished it off.

baslik: WordPress shows a blank white screen (White Screen of Death)
soru: My WordPress site is just a blank white page, no error, nothing, both the site and sometimes wp-admin. It happened after I installed/updated a plugin. I can't see any message to work with. How do I diagnose and recover a white screen?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: The White Screen of Death is usually a fatal PHP error that's being hidden because display_errors is off. The plugin you just touched is the prime suspect. First, turn on debugging to SEE the error: in wp-config.php set `define('WP_DEBUG', true);` and `define('WP_DEBUG_LOG', true);`, reload, then read wp-content/debug.log, it names the exact file/plugin and line.

If wp-admin also white-screens, deactivate plugins without the dashboard: via FTP/file manager, rename the wp-content/plugins folder to plugins_old. That deactivates all plugins; if the site comes back, rename it back and re-enable plugins one by one to find the culprit.

If it's not plugins, switch to a default theme the same way (rename the active theme folder so WordPress falls back to a default like Twenty Twenty-Four). A broken theme update causes identical symptoms.
A PHP memory exhaustion also causes white screens, raise it with `define('WP_MEMORY_LIMIT', '256M');` in wp-config.php. The debug log will say 'Allowed memory size exhausted' if that's the cause.

Enabling WP_DEBUG_LOG revealed a fatal error from the plugin I'd just updated (incompatible with my PHP version). Renaming its folder via FTP restored the site, then I updated PHP and reinstalled it cleanly.

First, turn on debugging to SEE the error: in wp-config.php set `define('WP_DEBUG', true);` and `define('WP_DEBUG_LOG', true);`, reload, then read wp-content/debug.log, it names the exact file/plugin and line.

baslik: 'Error establishing a database connection' suddenly appears
soru: My WordPress site shows 'Error establishing a database connection' and is completely down. It was working fine. I didn't change anything. What makes this appear out of nowhere and how do I get the site back?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: This means WordPress can't reach or log into its MySQL database. Three buckets: the DB credentials in wp-config.php are wrong/changed, the database server is down or overloaded, or the database tables are corrupted. Since 'nothing changed', the most common real cause is the DB server being down or hitting connection limits on shared hosting.

Check if the database server is up: many hosts kill MySQL when the account exceeds resource limits, or the DB host had an outage. Contact your host or check their status page. On shared hosting a traffic spike or a heavy plugin can exhaust DB connections and trip this intermittently.

Verify wp-config.php still has the correct DB_NAME, DB_USER, DB_PASSWORD and DB_HOST. Hosts occasionally change DB_HOST (e.g. from localhost to a specific server name) during migrations. Confirm the credentials by logging into phpMyAdmin with them.

If the DB is up and credentials are right, try repairing the database: add `define('WP_ALLOW_REPAIR', true);` to wp-config.php and visit yoursite.com/wp-admin/maint/repair.php, run the repair, then remove the line. Corrupted tables (often after a crash) cause exactly this.

Mine was the host's MySQL being down after they hit a resource limit; it returned on its own and I added caching so a traffic spike wouldn't exhaust DB connections again. Worth confirming credentials first though.

Three buckets: the DB credentials in wp-config.php are wrong/changed, the database server is down or overloaded, or the database tables are corrupted. Since 'nothing changed', the most common real cause is the DB server being down or hitting connection limits on shared hosting.

baslik: Locked out of wp-admin, login page reloads or rejects correct password
soru: I can't get into my WordPress admin. The login page either reloads back to itself without error, or rejects my password which I'm sure is correct. The front-end site works fine. How do I regain access to wp-admin?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: A login page that just reloads to itself (instead of erroring) is classically a cookie/redirect or a corrupted .htaccess / site URL mismatch. First, clear your browser cookies for the site and try an incognito window, stale cookies frequently cause the silent reload-loop.

If the password is genuinely rejected, reset it directly in the database via phpMyAdmin: in wp_users, edit your user's user_pass, set the function to MD5 and enter a new password, WordPress accepts MD5 on next login and re-hashes it. Or use the 'Lost your password?' email link if mail works.

A wrong Site URL causes login redirect loops: if siteurl/home in the database don't match how you're accessing the site (http vs https, www vs not), wp-admin bounces you. Set them correctly in wp_options (siteurl and home rows) or define WP_SITEURL/WP_HOME in wp-config.php.
A plugin (security/2FA/redirect plugins especially) can lock you out. Disable plugins via FTP by renaming the plugins folder, then try logging in; re-enable them one by one.
It was a stale session cookie plus an http/https mismatch in siteurl. Fixing the siteurl/home values and clearing cookies let me log straight in.

baslik: WordPress: 'Allowed memory size exhausted' fatal error
soru: I'm getting 'Fatal error: Allowed memory size of 134217728 bytes exhausted' on my WordPress site, sometimes in admin, sometimes on the front end. How do I increase WordPress's memory and is there an underlying problem I should worry about?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: That error means PHP hit its memory ceiling (here 128MB) mid-request. First raise it: add `define('WP_MEMORY_LIMIT', '256M');` to wp-config.php (and `WP_MAX_MEMORY_LIMIT` for admin). If your host caps PHP's memory_limit lower, you may also need to set it in php.ini or .user.ini, or ask the host to raise it.

But treat a sudden need for more memory as a symptom. A poorly-coded or conflicting plugin, or an import/backup operation, can consume memory abnormally. If 256MB gets exhausted too, something is leaking, find which plugin by deactivating and testing.

Enable WP_DEBUG_LOG to see exactly where the memory is consumed, the stack trace points at the plugin/theme function responsible. Often it's a page builder, a backup plugin, or an image-heavy operation.
Object caching and limiting heavy plugins reduce baseline memory. On shared hosting the real ceiling is the host's limit; if you constantly need more than they allow, you may have outgrown the plan.
Bumping WP_MEMORY_LIMIT to 256M stopped the immediate error, and the debug log showed a backup plugin was the heavy consumer, scheduling it off-peak and raising the limit resolved it.

If your host caps PHP's memory_limit lower, you may also need to set it in php.ini or .user.ini, or ask the host to raise it.

baslik: All posts return 404 after changing permalinks or migrating the site
soru: I changed my permalink structure (or moved the site to a new host) and now every post and page returns a 404, only the homepage works. The content is definitely still there. How do I fix the 404s on all my posts?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: This is the classic permalink/rewrite-rules issue. The simplest fix first: go to Settings > Permalinks and just click 'Save Changes' (without changing anything). That regenerates the rewrite rules and the .htaccess block, and resolves the 404s in the vast majority of cases.

If saving permalinks doesn't fix it, the web server isn't honoring the rewrite rules. On Apache, mod_rewrite must be enabled and the .htaccess must be writable and contain the WordPress rewrite block, AllowOverride must be set so .htaccess is read. After a migration these often get lost.

On Nginx there's no .htaccess, the rewrite must be in the server config: `try_files $uri $uri/ /index.php?$args;`. If you moved to an Nginx host, missing this rule makes every pretty permalink 404 while the homepage (index.php) still works, exactly your symptom.
Check the .htaccess file actually exists in the WordPress root and has the # BEGIN WordPress block; if file permissions stopped WordPress writing it, create it manually with the standard rules.
After my migration it was Nginx missing the try_files rule. Adding the standard WordPress location block fixed every 404. On Apache hosts, re-saving permalinks alone usually does it.

baslik: How do I keep my VS Code settings and extensions in sync across machines?
soru: I use VS Code on a work laptop and a home desktop and I'm constantly re-configuring settings, themes, keybindings and reinstalling extensions on each. Is there a built-in way to keep everything in sync between machines without manually copying files around?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: VS Code has Settings Sync built in, no extension needed. Click the gear (bottom-left) > 'Turn on Settings Sync', or Ctrl+Shift+P > 'Settings Sync: Turn On'. Sign in with a GitHub or Microsoft account and it syncs settings, keybindings, extensions, snippets and UI state across every machine where you sign in.

You choose what syncs in the turn-on dialog (you can exclude, say, machine-specific settings). On the second machine, install VS Code, turn on Settings Sync with the same account, and your extensions and config download automatically.

For machine-specific overrides (different paths at work vs home), use the settings.json scopes, sync the user settings, and keep truly machine-specific values in workspace settings or behind the 'Settings Sync: ignored settings' list so they don't clobber each other.
If you prefer not to use the account-based sync, the older approach is the Settings Sync extension via a GitHub Gist, but the built-in feature has made that largely unnecessary.
Turning on the built-in Settings Sync with my GitHub account was all it took, signing in on the other machine pulled every extension and setting within a minute.

baslik: How do I find my headless Raspberry Pi's IP address on the network?
soru: I'm running my Pi headless (no monitor) and need its IP to SSH in, but I don't know what address the router gave it. I don't want to plug in a screen every time. What's a reliable way to find the Pi's IP from another computer?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: The easiest is the hostname: recent Raspberry Pi OS advertises itself over mDNS, so from another machine you can often just `ssh pi@raspberrypi.local` (or whatever hostname you set in Imager) without knowing the IP at all. This works on Mac/Linux and modern Windows out of the box.
If .local doesn't resolve, check your router's admin page, it lists connected devices (DHCP client list) with their hostnames and IPs; the Pi shows up as 'raspberrypi' or your chosen hostname.

From a terminal, scan the subnet: `nmap -sn 192.168.1.0/24` lists live hosts and often identifies the Pi by its Raspberry Pi Foundation MAC prefix (b8:27:eb / dc:a6:32 / e4:5f:01). That pinpoints it even with a custom hostname.
Best long-term: give the Pi a static IP or a DHCP reservation in your router (bind its MAC to a fixed address) so it's always at the same place and you never hunt for it again.
ssh pi@raspberrypi.local worked immediately for me via mDNS, and I then set a DHCP reservation on the router so the address never changes.

baslik: After moving WordPress to HTTPS, images/CSS break with mixed-content warnings
soru: I installed an SSL certificate and switched my WordPress site to HTTPS, but now the browser shows 'not secure' / a broken padlock, and some images and stylesheets don't load. The console mentions 'mixed content' being blocked. How do I fix the insecure resources?

cevaplar.cevap_metni: Mixed content means the page loads over HTTPS but references some resources (images, CSS, JS) with hardcoded http:// URLs, browsers block those for security, breaking your layout and the padlock. The fix is to update those old http URLs in the database to https.

First set both Site Address and WordPress Address to the https:// version in Settings > General. Then run a search-replace across the database to fix hardcoded references, the Better Search Replace plugin (or WP-CLI `wp search-replace 'http://site.com' 'https://site.com'`) updates posts, options and widgets safely. Always back up first.

Don't hand-edit the database serialized data with raw SQL REPLACE, it can break serialized arrays (widgets, theme options). Use a tool that handles serialization (Better Search Replace / WP-CLI) so the lengths stay valid.

For stubborn cases, the 'Really Simple SSL' plugin auto-rewrites insecure requests to https on the fly, a quick fix, though doing the proper database replace is cleaner long-term. Also force https with a redirect in .htaccess so visitors always land on the secure version.
Running WP-CLI search-replace from http to https across the database fixed every broken image and the padlock turned green. Setting both URLs to https in General settings first was essential.
